parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hello Kathy, how’s your dissertation on water pumps going?

Not too bad, thanks. I’m getting on well with the literature review now. And my lab work’s fine so far.

Oh, that’s good. Remember, you should aim to have your results section completed by the end of next month. So there’s plenty of time to finalize the whole thing by the summer deadline. Anyway, looks like you’re on track. I’ve been through your first chapter now and I was quite impressed.

Oh, that’s a relief.

Well, sometimes your sentences are a little long and over complex. But the overall structure of the piece is very clear. I’d recommend you get a critical friend to go through it with you. Then once you’ve built in citations of other work in the field, I think it’ll be pretty good.

Oh, thanks. I was pleased I decided to focus on water pumps.

You seem to be testing an appropriate range of pump designs. Lots of students make the mistake of either restricting their range too much or conversely not narrowing it down enough. You’ve managed to avoid those twin traps. However, I think you’d get more convincing results if you took some additional measurements. I’ve noted exactly what I mean on your work.

Yes, I thought that might be necessary and I know I need to get down to some more library work too.

Well, I don’t think that’s essential at the moment.

Oh, right. So what do you suggest I do next? Repeat my last experiment using different variables?

Well, you could have a word with James Higgins tomorrow. He’s coming here to give a lecture on hydraulics to the faculty and it would be a great chance to have a chat with him. Especially as your experimental work has drawn so heavily from his last article in the British engineering journal.

Oh, fantastic.

And you never know how successful a chat with him might turn out to be. I got my first research post when I was a final year student and asked a visiting professor to explain what he meant in some article he’d written. So I urge all my students to take any such opportunity that arises.

But times have changed. People like that are too busy to talk to mere students these days.

I don’t know about that. Anyway, is there anything else I can help with? Any practical information about layout perhaps?

Well, I suppose I’m a bit unsure about how the bibliography should be presented. Like you, I can just check what’s normally done in journal articles so that’s not something to bother you with. I’d welcome some guidance though about what I should or shouldn’t include in the appendices. I know some things. Some of my data tables or details of specs perhaps are not really needed in the main body of the text and I’m likely to be pushed for words there.

Okay, I can certainly help you with that. But it will take a while so can we deal with that next week? I’ve got that solar panel seminar to go to in a few minutes. There’s plenty of work you can be carrying on with in the meantime.

Sure, that’s no problem. I think I’ll go and investigate the latest version of the CAD software to see if it might help with my pump design experiments at all.

Before you go though, I’d like quickly to run through what you should be doing over the next few months not just for your dissertation, but also to help your chances of getting the research post you’d like. Is that okay with you?

Yes, that would be really helpful.

Well, you certainly need to become a member of the Mechanical Engineers Society and then you’ll be able to go along to their meetings. There you must make a point of making yourself known to various people like Professor Jones. He’s the current president and is very approachable.

Okay, so I could do some networking there.

Exactly. Also, I think you should try to set up some visits to industry. Go to a lot of different workplaces just to see how things are done. It’s actually a very good way of making sure you’re familiar with the cutting edge of what’s going on. Textbooks, even academic articles, sometimes lag behind industry.

That sounds really interesting. Also, I’d love the chance to do a bit of work abroad for a while.

Well, that’s actually the next thing I was going to recommend. I’m sure we could set up a month for you in either the States or Canada, and that would be a great way to find out how things are done elsewhere.

That would be good, thank you.

And the last thing I was going to suggest was that you could go to the European Water Engineering Conference being held in Spain in May.

I could even present my dissertation there. Yes. Ah, thank you so much, that’s all really helpful.

Good.

analyses.content: Well, sometimes your sentences are a little long and over complex. But the overall structure of the piece is very clear. I’d recommend you get a critical friend to go through it with you. Then once you’ve built in citations of other work in the field, I think it’ll be pretty good.

导师称赞女生文章的“整体结构非常清晰（overall structure... is very clear）”，完美同义替换了选项A的“组织结构（organisation）”。

questions.question: going to Mechanical Engineers' Society meetings

analyses.content:
Well, you certainly need to become a member of the Mechanical Engineers Society and then you’ll be able to go along to their meetings. There you must make a point of making yourself known to various people like Professor Jones. He’s the current president and is very approachable.
Okay, so I could do some networking there.
Exactly.
如果你对“networking（拓展人脉）”这个词不熟悉，就很难把它和选项里的“contacts（联系人/人脉）”挂上钩，这里考查的是职场场景的高频同义替换。
导师建议她去学会的会议上让别人认识自己，女生也总结说可以在那里“拓展人脉（networking）”，完美对应选项F的“结交有用的人脉（make useful contacts）”。

Also, I think you should try to set up some visits to industry. Go to a lot of different workplaces just to see how things are done. It’s actually a very good way of making sure you’re familiar with the cutting edge of what’s going on. Textbooks, even academic articles, sometimes lag behind industry.
你可能会听到“workplaces”就想去选和“实践经验”相关的干扰项，但这里导师强调的核心落脚点是教科书往往落后，要去实地看最新的行业动态。
导师指出参观各种工作场所能确保你熟悉当前正在发生的“前沿动态（cutting edge）”，对应选项C的“保持最新状态（keeping up-to-date）”。

Well, that’s actually the next thing I was going to recommend. I’m sure we could set up a month for you in either the States or Canada, and that would be a great way to find out how things are done elsewhere.
That would be good, thank you.
这里的同义替换比较隐蔽，录音里用平实的大白话（了解其他地方怎么做事）替换了选项里偏学术的书面表达（拓宽实践经验），容易因为没抓准核心含义而漏选。
导师建议女生去美国或加拿大待一个月，因为这是了解其他地方“如何做事（how things are done elsewhere）”的好方法，对应选项A的“拓宽该领域的实践经验”。

And the last thing I was going to suggest was that you could go to the European Water Engineering Conference being held in Spain in May.
I could even present my dissertation there. Yes. Ah, thank you so much, that’s all really helpful.
这道题的答案是由女生自己主动抛出来的，如果你只顾着听导师的长篇大论，忽略了女生的兴奋回应，就会彻底错过这个得分点。
女生听到去参加西班牙的水利工程会议后，激动地表示自己甚至可以在那里“展示自己的论文（present my dissertation）”，直接对应选项B的“宣传自己的工作”。
